subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw define a public plugin-SDK dreaming protocol and runtime orchestration contract for memory plugins, or keep dreaming orchestration plugin-owned through ClawHub plugins?
rationale: Current main and releases only provide selected-slot config plus a memory-core sidecar, while a real provider protocol would add public SDK, config, scheduler, migration, and compatibility obligations.

options.title: Design SDK protocol with role-slot work
options.body: Define a documented dreaming provider contract after or alongside memory role slots, keeping memory-core as the default implementation and adding upgrade-safe docs/tests.

options.title: Keep dreaming plugin-owned
options.body: Document that alternate dreaming implementations should ship as ClawHub plugins and that OpenClaw core only exposes the current selected-slot config behavior.

options.title: Defer until PR #88504 settles
options.body: Leave this issue open but pause implementation until the memory role-slot PR lands or closes, then revisit the lifecycle/provider API shape.

recommendation.title: Design SDK protocol with role-slot work
recommendation.body: Define a documented dreaming provider contract after or alongside memory role slots, keeping memory-core as the default implementation and adding upgrade-safe docs/tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting public API and product-boundary decision, and @steipete is the listed project decision owner in CONTRIBUTING.md.
